- **Epoch labels:** the tip likely runs about 9.5 true epochs, not 8.5 (K_epochs).

- **Transfer to the PCIe judge:** a new Lvl2, K_judge, with a fresh-build reshuffle test (K_judge_build).

new.statement: On the E016 recipe, cutting weight decay further, to ×0.25 of the original, on the SGD groups only (BN biases, whitening bias, head), with Muon-filter wd left at E016's value, raises 3-seed mean accuracy by at least 0.2 pp over E016 at unchanged time.

E016's gain comes from the SGD groups, not the Muon filters. Starting from E016, restoring the original wd on the Muon conv filters only keeps 3-seed mean accuracy within 0.15 pp of E016. (First check in the code whether the port renormalizes filters as airbench94_muon does; if it does, filter wd is inert.)

On the E016 recipe, replacing Muon with Nesterov SGD (lr and wd scaled for batch 2000, with all other settings unchanged) lowers 3-seed mean accuracy by at least 0.3 pp. This would attribute E006's gain to Muon rather than to the batch-size change.

Cutting Muon per-step cost on the E016 recipe cuts mean time by at least 1.5% and keeps 3-seed mean accuracy within 0.2 pp. The means are reducing Newton-Schulz iterations from the current count (verify; reference 5) to 3, or, if filters are renormalized, renormalizing only every k steps with k rising over training as in Hiverge.

On the E016 recipe, adding a 20 px phase over the first ~15% of steps while keeping at least 30% of steps at 32 px (single-factor change vs E011) cuts mean time by at least 4% and loses no more than 0.25 pp of 3-seed mean accuracy.

Part of E011's accuracy cliff comes from end-of-run calibration rather than feature learning: the EMA weights and BN running stats average over low-res phases. On an E011-style schedule, recomputing BN stats at 32 px on ≤5k training images after the EMA swap (timed, <0.15 s) recovers at least 0.3 pp.
Size-dependent regularization helps: on the E016 recipe, using LS 0.1 during the 24/28 px phases and 0.3 at 32 px raises 3-seed mean accuracy by at least 0.2 pp at unchanged time.

With systems overhead exhausted and step time proportional to conv FLOPs, cutting FLOPs per sample through architecture (convs per group, group-1/2 widths aligned to tensor-core tiles) trades time for accuracy at a better rate than cutting epochs, i.e. more than 2 s per pp.
On the E016 recipe, narrowing group 2 from 384 to 320 channels cuts mean time by at least 5% and loses no more than 0.25 pp of 3-seed mean accuracy.
On the E016 recipe, dropping the third conv in group 1 (the group run at the highest resolution) cuts mean time by at least 8% and loses no more than 0.4 pp of 3-seed mean accuracy.

Profiling one 32 px batch-2000 step of the E016 recipe shows an achieved rate of at least 90 TFLOP/s, in line with airbench's 110–116 TFLOP/s. That would leave no kernel-efficiency lever worth more than 5%.

The epoch labels are off. Reading the step count from the E016 commit shows total optimizer steps of about 9.5 × (50000/2000), not 8.5 epochs. The same off-by-about-one error applies to E004/E005 (10 epochs, not 9).

A two-point trim of E016 (−0.5 and −1.0 true epochs, LR/EMA/resize schedules stretched to the step count) cuts each 0.5 epoch for 0.1–0.45 pp of 3-seed mean accuracy and ~5% time, and the −0.5 point stays at or above 0.7545.

Run offline on held-out seeds 3–12, the E016 recipe gives a 10-seed mean of at least 0.757 and between 0.05 and 0.3 pp below its seeds-0–2 mean of 0.7607 (winner's-curse offset from keep decisions made on seeds 0–2).

Local SXM4 results transfer to the PCIe judge only partly. The time ranking holds because the step is GPU-bound, but the judge's own max-autotune pass picks different kernels, so per-seed trajectories reshuffle. Accuracy must therefore be budgeted as an expectation with at least 0.3 pp headroom over 0.75 on the 40-seed mean.
Building the E016 max-autotune/cudagraph recipe twice in fresh processes gives per-seed accuracies that are not bit-identical in at least one seed, with a 3-seed mean shift of no more than 0.25 pp.
